title: Branch-search connector results are not exhaustive branch inventory evidence

observed: Repository metadata identifies the default branch as main.
Two branch-search calls against MirrorCartographer/mirror-cartographer-ui returned an empty result set, including a query for main.
Recent commit search continued to return commits from the repository during the same run.
inferred: An empty branch-search connector result cannot establish that the repository has no branches.
The branch-search endpoint is unsuitable as the sole exhaustive-coverage mechanism for M-RECONCILE-002 under the observed connector behavior.
proposed: Require an independently retained branch enumeration from an authenticated Git traversal or a GitHub refs endpoint that returns the known default branch before classifying branch coverage as complete.
superseded: Treating a zero-result branch-search response as exhaustive absence evidence.
unresolved: The complete branch inventory remains unknown.
The provenance and immutable locations of M-004, M-005, and M-006 remain unresolved.
The originating source that assigned those identifiers remains unlocated.

contradiction_resolution.apparent_contradiction: Repository metadata names main while branch search returns no branches.
contradiction_resolution.resolution: The zero-result search is classified as a connector capability or indexing limitation, not repository absence.

falsification_route: Produce an authenticated, retained refs or git-for-each-ref enumeration that includes main and proves pagination or traversal completeness.
